newsitem.title: Austria: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL CALLED OFF.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL CALLED OFF.

text.p: Heavy fog and poor visibility led to a women's Alpine skiing World Cup downhill race being called off on Friday.
Organisers were forced to halt the season's third downhill, which started one hour and 45 minutes late because of heavy snowfalls, after only seven racers had come down the Strohsack piste.
Friday's race was supposed to be the replacement for a downhill which was called off in Crans Montana, Switzerland, in December because of bad weather.

Organisers in Bad Kleinkirchheim decided to postpone Friday's race until Saturday, when another downhill is already scheduled. They now plan to hold two downhills on the 3,010-metre long Strohsack piste on Saturday, starting at 1100 and 1300 local time (1000 and 1200 GMT) respectively.
The Austrian resort is also due to host a super-giant slalom on Sunday, weather permitting.

France's Florence Masnada was leading with a time of one minute 44.78 seconds before the interruption. Germany's Hilde Gerg was lying second in 1:45.29 and France's Regine Cavagnoud was in third place with 1:46.23.
